## Intent
Hypothesis: compiler auto-vectorization of the per-particle integration loop can recover streaming-level throughput despite AoS layout.

## Layout & approach
The AoS Particle struct is 68 B/particle. Loop 1 touches 24 of 68 B (35% hot), loop 2 touches 8 of 68 B (11% hot), loop 3 touches 28 of 68 B (41% hot) — the rest is dead weight dragged through cache lines. No intermediate storage is allocated; the death verdict stays in registers. The approach expects the compiler to auto-vectorize loop 1's component math over stride-68, but the hot fractions mean 59–89% of fetched bandwidth is wasted depending on the loop. All measured N exceed the L1d spill (N≈481) and L2 spill (N≈7710); N=10000–100000 are L3-resident, N≥1000000 are DRAM.

## Cache saturation
At q=0.01, ns/p is flat at ~25.3 across L3-resident N=10000–100000, then rises to ~29–30 at the DRAM transition — a ~4–5 ns/p knee at the L3→DRAM boundary. Higher death rates shift the entire curve up (q=0.5: ~33–37 ns/p) without changing the transition shape, because respawn overhead is frontend-bound, not cache-dependent. The L3-resident regime is flat between N=10000 and N=100000, confirming comfortable L3 residency with no sub-structure.

## Bandwidth
Achieved bandwidth is 1.8–2.69 GB/s against a 12.69 GB/s ceiling — 14–21% of capacity. The memory floor is 5.359 ns/p; the algo runs 4.7–7.1x above it. This is frontend/overhead-bound: frontend stalls dominate at 64–75%, compute at 14–35%, branch_flush at 0.0%. Against baseline it is flat at 0.96–1.125x naive scalar — auto-vectorization delivered no speedup. Against the winner it is 1.9–3.3x slower, narrowing at high q (3.28x at q=0.01 N=10000 vs 1.92x at q=0.5 N=10000) because the winner's optimized respawn also degrades.

## Assembly
Vector-suffixed instructions total 0 — no cross-particle vectorization. Loop 1 processes one particle per iteration at stride 0x44 (68 bytes) using scalar SSE (`vmulss`, `vaddss`) with intra-particle packed ops (`vmulps`, `vaddps`, `vshufps`, `vinsertps`) on 3–4 component vectors loaded via `vmovups`/`vmovsd`. Loop 2 is branchy: `vucomiss`/`jae` death check, `call` to spawn, inline RNG with `lzcnt`/`rorx`. Loop 3 does byte-granular stores (`mov BYTE PTR`) with `vcvttss2si` and `cmovae` clamping to 0xff. The 64–75% frontend stalls stem from this scalar control flow and stride-68 access defeating prefetch-friendly streaming.

## Verdict
Refuted — 0 vector-suffixed instructions, 0.96–1.125x baseline and 1.9–3.3x slower than the winner at every N×q point. The stride-68 AoS layout defeated auto-vectorization; intra-particle packed ops (`vmulps`, `vaddps`) cannot compensate. Frontend stalls at 64–75% cap bandwidth at 14–21% of ceiling, 4.7–7.1x above the memory floor, regardless of death rate.
